questionByQuestionAnalysis.question: Design a distributed rate limiter
questionByQuestionAnalysis.candidateAnswer: We use Redis sliding window with sorted sets keyed by client IP, using Lua scripts for atomic ZREMRANGEBYSCORE and ZADD.
whatYouDidWell: Atomic Lua script and sliding window mechanics correctly explained
whatWasMissing: Deeper exploration of edge cases and scale considerations.
deductionReasons: Minor deductions for missing production boundary considerations.
questionByQuestionAnalysis.howToImprove: Structure answers with explicit trade-off comparisons.
questionByQuestionAnalysis.bestPossibleAnswer: To architect a distributed rate limiter for 50k RPS across multiple data centers: employ Redis cluster with the Token Bucket or Sliding Window Counter algorithm executed via atomic Lua scripts to prevent distributed race conditions. To avoid cross-region network latency on every request, implement localized Redis instances with asynchronous reconciliation or use local token buckets combined with centralized quota allocation tokens.
